Empires & Puzzles Cathal Review: Is The Bravehearted Slayer Still Sharp?

Cathal hits like a freight train... eventually. We revisit this Slayer of Fell Shadows to see if his massive sword and bypassing strikes can still cut it in a world of Magic speed and Mega Minions. Is he a sleeper hit for Rush Attack, or just a slow-motion relic?
Cathal: The Barbarian Who Forgot to Bring His Running Shoes
Cathal: The Locomotive That Takes a While to Leave the Station
Cathal, known as "The Bravehearted," is a 5-star Ice hero from the

event. Released back in 2021, he represents a unique era of Empires & Puzzles where "Slow" mana speed was balanced by high damage and a mechanic designed to ramp up over time. As a member of the Slayer family, he doesn't just hit you; he plans to hit you faster and harder the longer you let him live. He is the quintessential "momentum" hero—useless if dead early, but a runaway train if left unchecked.

Let's be honest: Cathal is pure, unfiltered 80s fantasy cheese, and we love it. He channels serious Conan the Barbarian energy, complete with the "Arnold" jawline, scars, and a sword that looks too heavy to lift, let alone swing. The art screams "brute force." While newer heroes are draped in neon magic and particle effects, Cathal is just a shirtless dude with a really big piece of metal. It’s a grounded, gritty aesthetic that fits his "Breaker Blade" persona perfectly.
To put it bluntly, Cathal's stats are showing their age. With a base power of 811, he is significantly behind modern heroes who regularly push past 1250+ power.

Upon release, Cathal was a monster. He had the highest power in the game and could one-shot almost anyone. The "Slow" speed was a fair trade-off for his ability to bypass the ubiquitous Sif and Krampus metas of the time.

The game has left him behind. Modern heroes do more damage at Fast speed than Cathal does at Slow. The "ramp up" mechanic takes too long for standard raids where matches are often decided in the first 4-5 turns.
He is largely obsolete for competitive PvP (Raids/War) unless you are playing in

wars/tournaments. In Rush, his speed drawback is negated, and his bypass is excellent against the defensive buffs common in that mode. He is also usable on Titans due to high single-target damage if you lack newer options.

If you pull Cathal early, he is a great "Boss Killer" for map stages. His self-healing and damage reduction will help you survive hard levels. However, do not prioritize him over a solid healer or a Fast sniper if you have one. He requires patience to use effectively.

The community had mixed feelings about Cathal from day one.
"This guy is insane! like a Cobalt but with massive defense... Quite scary!" -
"To me he is the worst 5* of this event. He just has pure snipe damage which is garbage at slow speed." -
"By Krum… This is Conan the barbarian. Arnold’s in the game. So powerful." -
History has proven the skeptics right regarding the speed, but the fans right regarding the "cool factor."

Cathal is a relic of a simpler time. A time when a big shirtless man with a big sword was enough to strike fear into the hearts of enemies. Today, he's a bit like bringing a broadsword to a drone fight. He's cool, he hits hard if he connects, but he's often taken out before he gets within swinging range. Keep him for Rush Attack or the nostalgia, but don't expect him to carry your team to the Top 100.
